_comment: Every command is wrapped in the bootstrap guard prosthetic-conscience established: a fresh plugin-cache version ships from git WITHOUT binaries (they arrive via doctor --fix), and an unguarded hook crash-storms every tool call in that window. The guard degrades to ONE stderr line pointing at the fix. SessionStart records where the MAIN session's transcript is — SubagentStop only ever hands over a SEAT's, so without this row a consumer has no non-guessing way to find the session's own trajectory (plans/gray-area.md §11.2). The event is passed with -event rather than inferred from the payload: the wiring already knows which hook it registered for. Stop and SessionEnd feed the CATALOGUE and write no manifest row: Stop is the turn boundary, where a session's own transcript has just grown, and SessionEnd is the last chance to read it before the session is gone. Their cost is the read of one file's tail, not a reprojection.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/gray-area-capture"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event SubagentStop; fi; echo 'gray-area: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/gray-area-capture"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event SessionStart; fi; echo 'gray-area: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/gray-area-capture"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event Stop; fi; echo 'gray-area: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/gray-area-capture"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event SessionEnd; fi; echo 'gray-area: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2
